newsitem.title: JAPAN: Prosecutors arrest former DKB chairman Okuda - NHK.
newsitem.headline: Prosecutors arrest former DKB chairman Okuda - NHK.

text.p: Tokyo prosecutors have arrested a former chairman of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Tadashi Okuda, in connection with a growing payoff scandal involving racketeers and Nomura Securities, Japan's biggest securities house, NHK television reported on Friday.

NHK said Okuda was arrested on suspicion that he was involved in arranging illegal payments that the bank made to Ryuichi Koike, a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer who is a central figure in the scandal.
The report of the arrest followed the suicide last week of Okuda's predecessor Kuniji Miyazaki.
Miyazaki died on June 29 after hanging himself at his home two days after prosecutors started questioning him over his role in the payoff scandal.

Prosecutors considered Miyazaki and Okuda key figures in their investigation of the scandal involving DKB and Nomura. Both firms are believed by prosecutors to have made illegal payoffs to racketeers.
Earlier that week, four former executives of DKB were indicted on charges of making illegal payments to Koike. They were the first Dai-Ichi Kangyo executives to be indicted in the case.
